findings.title: Freeze immutable public field types and replay outcome invariants
findings.trigger: A caller constructs BundleManifest or ReplayReport using the advertised public records. Field names are listed, but versions has no specified immutable in-memory representation/type, and several ReplayReport scalar/null types and status-state combinations remain unspecified at line41.
findings.consequence: Independent implementations can choose incompatible mutable dictionaries vs tuples/frozen version records, or accept contradictory report states such as matched with a nonverified compatibility/content state. The promise of exact known immutable records and meaningful typed outcomes is not yet a complete constructor contract.
findings.requested_change: Before Ready freeze exact public field types/tuple limits/ordering (especially BundleManifest.versions), ReplayReport scalar bounds and a closed outcome matrix mapping each status to execution/content/compatibility states, count, timing/match/output nullability. Add independent direct-constructor negatives for contradictory combinations.

findings.title: Specify literal lexical token limits before JSON parsing
findings.trigger: A stored typed entry fits the32MiB aggregate and node/depth limits but contains one enormous integer token or escaped string token. The plan says number/string preflight exists but freezes no token grammar/length/counting rule before JSON loads or float.fromhex.
findings.consequence: The parser/reconstructor can materialize or process far larger primitive tokens than typed-json-v1 permits, and exact boundary/error fixtures cannot be independently specified from this packet. Post-reconstruction width/label checks do not establish the promised pre-parser admission rule.
findings.requested_change: Freeze conservative raw-token and decoded-string counting bounds and canonical numeric grammar before loads: e.g. typed integers at most38digits plus optionalminus with abs<10^38, bounded float64-hex strings before conversion, separate manifest/receipt integer rules, and bounded escaped payload/label tokens with surrogates rejected. State deterministic rejection and exact-limit/one-over tests. These remain application controls, not physical quotas.
